chunks: Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
'Completion of the Quran is up to where you know.'

key_terms.تَعْلَمُ: You know — referring to comprehension, familiarity, and understanding of the text being recited
key_terms.خَتْمُ الْقُرْآنِ: Khatm al-Quran — the completion or sealing of a full recitation of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about completing the Quran recitation?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) taught that the completion (khatm) of the Quran is measured not by mechanical recitation but by the reciter's comprehension — 'up to where you know.' This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq from his father Imam al-Baqir, emphasizes the spiritual and intellectual dimension of Quranic recitation. The early Muslim community understood this to mean that one should recite with understanding and reflection, not mere repetition of words one does not comprehend.
